bug_semantics: With channels.msteams.groupPolicy set to allowlist, a configured teams/team/channel route allowlist was incorrectly treated as sufficient authorization when the effective sender groupAllowFrom list was empty. A message from any sender in a matched route therefore passed the route gate and skipped the sender gate, allowing an unauthorized Teams group sender to trigger bot processing and replies.
flaw_origin: Commit c7ea47e88682283f87cb8d6481df67f4def0258f added Teams route allowlisting and changed the empty-sender-allowlist rejection from an unconditional effectiveGroupAllowFrom.length === 0 check to effectiveGroupAllowFrom.length === 0 && !channelGate.allowlistConfigured. That conflated route authorization with sender authorization and first created the bypass. Commit 27dad962fee567e50ed7e293a4d8eb67cc7da8e6 later preserved the same behavior while refactoring it into an explicit ["*"] sender list; it was not the behavioral introducer.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object names human author and committer Peter Steinberger <steipete@gmail.com>; its message is only 'feat(channels): add resolve command + defaults' and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI trailer, and neither identity is a bot.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/security/advisories/GHSA-g7cr-9h7q-4qxq describes the Microsoft Teams route/sender allowlist bypass, marks openclaw <= 2026.3.7 affected and >= 2026.3.8 patched, and identifies fix 88aee9161e0e6d32e810a25711e32a808a1777b2.

git show 88aee9161e0e6d32e810a25711e32a808a1777b2 -- extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts shows the direct fix replacing the conditional wildcard expression with groupAllowFrom: effectiveGroupAllowFrom; the accompanying authz regression test sends attacker-aad into a configured team/channel route with groupAllowFrom: [] and requires conversationStore.upsert not to run.

git log -L 245,248:extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts 88aee9161e0e6d32e810a25711e32a808a1777b2^ follows the vulnerable behavior through 27dad962fee567e50ed7e293a4d8eb67cc7da8e6 back to c7ea47e88682283f87cb8d6481df67f4def0258f; -S'&& !channelGate.allowlistConfigured' returns the same BIC and the later refactor.

git show c7ea47e88682283f87cb8d6481df67f4def0258f -- extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts shows the BIC adding channelGate and weakening the empty sender-list rejection to effectiveGroupAllowFrom.length === 0 && !channelGate.allowlistConfigured, while checking sender identity only when effectiveGroupAllowFrom.length > 0.

Direct parent-tree verification: git grep at b54333937335674d7d3d4de8d35810c146d7ec26 finds extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:199 as unconditional 'if (effectiveGroupAllowFrom.length === 0)', whereas the BIC tree at line 219 adds '&& !channelGate.allowlistConfigured'. Thus the matched-route/empty-sender-list bypass is absent from the immediate parent.

git cat-file -p c7ea47e88682283f87cb8d6481df67f4def0258f shows one parent, human author/committer Peter Steinberger, and no trailers; GitHub's associated-pulls endpoint returns [], so there is no reconstructable squash/member history to substitute for this commit.

Version ancestry checks show c7ea47e88682283f87cb8d6481df67f4def0258f is an ancestor of vulnerable tag v2026.3.7, fix 88aee9161e0e6d32e810a25711e32a808a1777b2 is not an ancestor of v2026.3.7, and the fix is an ancestor of patched tag v2026.3.8. git describe --contains places the BIC before v2026.1.20 and the fix before v2026.3.8-beta.1.
reasoning: The authorization boundary has two independent dimensions: the team/channel route must be allowed, and under groupPolicy=allowlist the sender must be present in the effective sender allowlist. Before c7ea47e88682283f87cb8d6481df67f4def0258f, an empty effectiveGroupAllowFrom always caused an early return. The BIC introduced route allowlisting and made that return conditional on no route allowlist being configured, so a matched route plus an empty sender list continued without any sender check. Later commit 27dad962fee567e50ed7e293a4d8eb67cc7da8e6 merely restated this already-vulnerable behavior by passing ["*"] to a shared evaluator. The fix removed that synthesis and always passed the real effectiveGroupAllowFrom, restoring empty-list rejection. Parent-tree and tag ancestry checks establish the introduction and affected/patched boundaries. Because only the smallest behavioral BIC may determine AI attribution and its commit object contains no AI or bot marker, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
